On DRC ethnic diversity: the Congolese government's efforts are limited; political elites exploit ethnic differences, and deep ethnic tensions/mistrust persist. #DRC #ethnic-diversity

DRC's constitution recognizes the country's diversity, and the government created institutions to promote unity and reconciliation; the National Solidarity Fund for the Reconstruction of the DRC (FNSRDC) was created in 2001 to address root causes of conflict including ethnic divisions. #DRC #FNSRDC
DRC has quotas for women and marginalized populations in parliament but no ethnic quotas; it also uses affirmative action in public-service hiring and promotions to increase diversity. #DRC #quotas

DRC civil society groups working on ethnic diversity: Ligue des Electeurs (League of Voters — democracy, fair elections, ethnic discrimination in electoral process); Nkumu Fed Fed (grassroots, cultural rights of minorities incl. Bantu and Pygmy peoples, representation in decision-making). #DRC #civil-society

Other DRC civil society groups on ethnic diversity: Voix des Femmes pour la Paix (Voice of Women for Peace — women's rights in peacebuilding); Centre de Recherche et de Promotion des Initiatives Locales de Développement (sustainable development, social cohesion in conflict-affected communities); Conférence Episcopale Nationale du Congo / CENCO (Catholic Church-backed, peacebuilding and reconciliation). #DRC #civil-society

DRC civil society orgs get little to no government support or funding, partly due to limited state resources and government suspicion of critical NGOs; they depend on international donors and face intimidation/harassment. #DRC #civil-society #funding
In 2018 the DRC government passed a law restricting foreign-funded organizations, requiring them to register with the government and get approval for their programs. #DRC #NGO-law

Ways individuals outside the DRC can support Congolese civil society: donate to organizations, raise awareness (social media, articles, community talks), volunteer (fundraising, advocacy, technical support), and advocate for policy change by their own governments. #DRC #civil-society #support

Ligue des Electeurs (League of Voters) is a DRC NGO promoting democracy, justice and stability, active on fair elections and ethnic discrimination/marginalization in the electoral process. #DRC #civil-society
Nkumu Fed Fed is a DRC grassroots movement promoting cultural rights of minority groups including Bantu and Pygmy peoples, and their representation in decision-making. #DRC #civil-society
Voix des Femmes pour la Paix (Voice of Women for Peace) is a DRC civil society organization focused on women's rights and women's participation in peacebuilding. #DRC #civil-society

Centre de Recherche et de Promotion des Initiatives Locales de Développement is a DRC civil society group promoting sustainable development and social cohesion in conflict-affected communities. #DRC #civil-society
Conférence Episcopale Nationale du Congo (CENCO), backed by the Catholic Church, has long been involved in peacebuilding and reconciliation in the DRC. #DRC #civil-society
